names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 2 Ιουνίου, «Άγιος Ανδρέας πρίγκιπας της Σουζδαλίας», with the rank word left off. The Russian form of his name is not printed on the page and is not invented here.

death.note: saint.gr's head line reads «Αγιος Ανδρεας Πριγκιπας Της Σουζδαλιας (; - 1365)» and the life says he fell asleep in peace in 1365. The page gives no year of birth; it dates his father's death to 1355, his accession to that year and his abdication to 1359.

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding Julian day (1 October 2026). He is a Russian prince and the Russian calendar is the one that would know him, but no Russian source was opened for this draft.
Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (1 October 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 2ης Ιουνίου — «Άγιος Ανδρέας πρίγκιπας της Σουζδαλίας»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 2 Ιουνίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. The page names Suzdal, Nizhny Novgorod and Gorodets as the principalities he was given and Russia as his country; `locations` is left out because three principalities are not one point. The corpus keeps no prince of Suzdal and no other Andrew of the fourteenth century. The date is the Greek calendar's; that a Russian prince stands in it on a revised-julian day is the Greek calendar's own reckoning and is recorded as read.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue on pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (1 October 2026).
